Christoph Lameter demonstrated very poor scalability on the SGI 512-way
a many-threaded application which concurrently initializes different parts of
a large anonymous area.
This patch corrects that
column2: by using a separate spinlock per page table page

column1: guard the page table entries in that page
column2: instead of using the mm's single

column1: page_table_lock.  (But even then
column2: page_table_lock is still used to guard page

column1: table allocation
In this implementation
column2: the spinlock is tucked inside the struct page of the

column1: page table page: with a BUILD_BUG_ON in case it overflows - which it would in
the case of 32-bit PA-RISC with spinlock debugging enabled.
Splitting the lock is not quite for free: another cacheline access.  Ideally
I suppose we would use split ptlock only for multi-threaded processes on
multi-cpu machines; but deciding that dynamically would have its own costs.
So for now enable it by config
column2: at some number of cpus - since the Kconfig

column1: language doesn't support inequalities
NR_CPUS.  But I don't think it's worth being user-configurable: for good
testing of both split and unsplit configs
change that to 8 later.
There is a benefit even for singly threaded processes: kswapd can be attacking
one part of the mm while another part is busy faulting.
